claim_verbatim: Nothing changes our current trajectory, and to complicate matters further, nobody really knows what trajectory we're on; we just have models that approximate it, and they aren't very predictive. Climate models are so coarse that we know little beyond the fact that the climate is heating. We don't really know the true rate of heating (the models we had underestimated the rate) , which suggests we are accelerating toward significant change and that the models tell us significant change probably looks like a reversion to the Younger Dryas climate era. About 12,800 years ago, we entered the Holocene era; that era has seen a relatively stable climate. Now we probably enter a new era . Climate change action or no action  is a political discourse
context: X reply to @brengang010 (thread with @tanya_plibersek), after his reply to Plibersek that her policies do nothing to mitigate climate change.
